title: “Grillz on a hijabi”: Intersectional Identities in Fostering Critical AI Literacy
findings: The generative AI model struggled to accurately represent Muslim religious attire and cultural concepts. It often generated images of hijabs that failed to meet modesty standards (e.g., showing bangs) and produced abayas that were inappropriately revealing. Culturally specific terms like 'Khaleeji' were misinterpreted and defaulted to male images, showing gender bias. Participants had to explicitly add terms like 'modest' or 'hijab' to prompts to get culturally appropriate outputs, and even then, the AI defaulted to generating images of White models. These failures prompted the participants to critically analyze AI bias, connecting it to the limitations of training data and developer assumptions.

measurement_description: The study measured how well a generative AI model could represent the intersectional identities of Black Muslim teen girls, specifically focusing on its ability to generate culturally and religiously appropriate fashion designs, such as hijabs and abayas, and its biases in representing race and modesty.
